result.title: 1. Introduction
result.summary: FPIF seeks proposals for non-discretionary private-markets consulting and approximately three discretionary OCIO advisory mandates; forms and updates are on its website, which respondents must monitor. Created by Illinois to manage investments for about 300 local firefighter pension funds, FPIF is Pension Code-governed, has a nine-member board, and managed $7.6 billion as of January 2023. Its private-markets target is 31%: 10% private equity, 7% debt, 10% real estate, and 4% infrastructure. The consultant covers sourcing and recommendations across all classes; discretionary advisors manage higher-risk segments: Private Equity (4%), Real Assets (including 2.5% debt and 5% real estate), and Opportunistic Strategies (3% equity and 2.5% debt), with allocations subject to change and possible staff veto or pipeline involvement. Requirements span fund types, strategies, sizes, returns, benchmarks, global access, niche/opportunistic credit and real assets, emerging managers, and institutional solutions. FPIF prefers separate accounts except potentially venture fund-of-funds. The RFP also states FPIF’s goal, under state law, to promote racial, ethnic, and gender diversity among fiduciaries and investment vendors.

result.title: 2. Proposal Content
key_items: 2.3. Minimum Qualifications Certification; 2.4. Description of Respondent’s Experience and Qualifications; 2.5. References; 2.6. Fee Proposal; 2.7 Additional Documentation and Data
2.4. Description of Respondent’s Experience and Qualifications
result.summary: Proposals must include every Section 2 component, preferably in a zip file with a table of contents and each component separately organized; failure to follow the format may result in rejection. The signed business-letter proposal cover letter must identify an authorized signer and state compliance, truthfulness and completeness, offer validity for up to 360 days after the due date, disclose specified relationships or negotiations, acknowledge possible public disclosure, identify all proposal documents, certify no fraud, collusion or related remuneration, and accept Exhibit A certifications and terms. Complete Exhibit B in order, repeating each full question and number and answering independently; complete Exhibit C minimum-qualifications certification. Describe consulting/advisory history, AUM/AUA overall and in proposed asset classes, investment inception dates, lead consultant/CIO experience, subcontracted services and selection/monitoring, and team roles. Provide three references, including a public defined-benefit plan, with contact details and appropriate investment staff; FPIF may contact them. Include all-inclusive Exhibit D fees and Exhibit E materials. Proposals may become public under Illinois FOIA; claimants must identify and label confidential pages, specify and justify applicable exemptions, and flag confidential content in the submission email. FPIF decides confidentiality.

result.title: 3. Timeline and Submission Requirements
result.summary: The procurement timeline is subject to FPIF’s discretion; updates will be posted on its website, which respondents should check. Key dates: RFP issued February 13, 2023; written questions due February 24 by noon Central; answers posted March 3; proposals due March 10 by noon Central; possible interviews in Q2–Q3 2023 and presentations in Q3–Q4; anticipated Consultant selection May 26 and Discretionary Advisor selection August 25. Proposals must follow the RFP and be emailed as PDFs by the deadline to Mitchell Green (mgreen@ifpif.org) and investments@ifpif.org. Use the subject “Response to FPIF Private Markets Consulting and Advisory RFP – (Name of Respondent)”; unclear subject lines may cause rejection. Late proposals may not be considered. Email is the only accepted submission method, and receipt will be confirmed. Proposals may be withdrawn before the deadline by signed written notice from the applicant or authorized agent, referencing the RFP title; withdrawal will be confirmed. Modified proposals may be resubmitted by the deadline, but other forms of modification will not be considered.

result.title: 4. Procurement Rules and Procedure
key_items: 4.1. Procurement Rules; 4.2. Communications; Quiet Period; 4.3. Procurement Contact
result.summary: FPIF’s adopted procurement rules and applicable law govern the process, overseen by staff and advisors; it will publish the selected Respondent and contract amount, fees, and selection factors. A quiet period runs from RFP issuance until selection or closure: no procurement-related ex parte contact or attempts to influence selection are allowed, except ordinary, unrelated communications with existing service providers. Questions must go by the stated deadline to Procurement Contact Mitchell Green (mgreen@ifpif.org); answers will be anonymized in a website Q&A, with no individual replies. Proposals are checked for completeness and accuracy; false or unsupported claims may be rejected. Compliant proposals are assessed for best value using experience, mandate fit, scale, team and stability, investment and sourcing capabilities, access, risk, performance, ESG/DEI, clients, price, alignment, ethics, references, location, and qualifying ownership status. FPIF may seek clarifications or verify qualifications, but post-deadline changes are restricted. Submissions become FPIF property and may be publicly disclosed. Respondents bear costs; the RFP is not an offer. FPIF reserves broad rights to reject, revise, cancel, waive or correct requirements, request revised offers, negotiate, and disqualify.

result.title: Exhibit A: Certifications and Terms Required by State Law
result.summary: Exhibit A lists 27 Illinois-law certifications and contract terms required of FPIF respondents; any inability must be explained in the proposal by item number, and the terms will be incorporated into an agreement. They cover ethics; bribery, securities-related felonies, state debt, use tax, environmental and lead-law violations; conflicts, financial disclosures, political contributions, drug-free workplaces, bid-rigging, boycotts, third-party fees, revolving-door rules, registration, and reporting anticompetitive conduct. They also require nondiscrimination, affirmative action and sexual-harassment policies; no support for discriminatory clubs; prevailing-wage compliance where applicable; seven-year transition records and audit access; reporting employee-solicitation plans; acknowledgment of open-records and open-meetings laws; representation that the respondent is not a specified Illinois finance entity; annual workforce and diverse-business contracting disclosures; ownership disclosures; and disclosure and ongoing notification of subcontractors, marketers, and their expected compensation, subject to stated exclusions.

result.title: Exhibit B: Questionnaire
result.summary: Exhibit B requires proposal respondents to reproduce each question before its answer and respond in order. It collects company, contact, entity, tax-ID certification, ownership, and control information. The questionnaire examines firm history, structure, offices, registrations, assets and clients, private-market services, business lines, growth, ownership and diversity; continuity, cybersecurity, insurance, conflicts, ESG, legal/regulatory matters, audits, and compliance. It requests workforce and investment-team details, qualifications, responsibilities, client service, diversity, turnover, succession, public roles, compliance leadership, and counsel. Strategy questions cover private equity, private debt, and real estate/infrastructure experience, investment approaches, sourcing and manager selection, due diligence, risk, allocations, relationships, market outlook, fees, competitive positioning, and performance. Required tables report fund and composite results, returns, multiples, and strategy metrics; questions also address capacity and comparable mandates. Operations topics include account availability and minimums, reporting timelines and samples, client tools, attribution, valuation and cash reconciliation, fee validation, and the firm’s suitability as an FPIF partner.

nodes.title: Proposal Questionnaire: Company, Contacts, and Ownership
nodes.summary: Exhibit B requires the completed questionnaire to accompany the proposal, with each question listed before its answer and responses kept in questionnaire order. It collects company name and mailing address, phone, fax, website, state, ZIP code, and a perjury certification of the Federal Employer Identification Number; respondents also identify their business entity type. Contact-person details include name, title, phone, fax, and email. Ownership information covers applicable organizational forms and, as required by Section 1-113.14(c) of the Pension Code, the names and addresses of parent or controlling entities, subsidiaries or entities controlled by the respondent, persons with ownership or distributive-income shares exceeding 7.5%, and the respondent’s executive officers.

nodes.title: Organization
nodes.summary: The RFP asks respondents to identify the contracting entity and proposed mandates; describe the firm’s founding, history, leadership, succession, strategy, institutional consulting and advisory experience, headquarters and offices, FPIF service locations, Illinois presence, SEC registration and ADV, organizational structure, and anticipated changes. It requests current and historical firm assets under advisement/management by year, asset class, mandate type, and client type, including private-market assets, client counts, market values, uncalled commitments, and explanations of “other.” Respondents must describe private-market products and services, advisory practices and differences between discretionary and non-discretionary work, access to high-demand funds, and success backing emerging top-quartile managers. Further questions cover client wins and losses, public-fund clients, growth plans, business lines and revenue, ownership and ownership changes, and minority, women, or disability ownership, MWDBE certification, and applicable Illinois business-enterprise status.

nodes.title: Firm Client Firm Private Market Count (#) AUA/AUM ($) AUA/AUM ($)
nodes.summary: The RFP requests information on the firm’s private-market products and services; advisory approach and differences between discretionary and non-discretionary mandates; access to high-demand funds and success backing top-quartile first- or second-fund managers. It seeks client-type AUA/AUM, explanation of “other,” five-year client gains/losses and mandate details, and public-fund clients and service history. It asks about three-to-five-year growth plans, other business lines and revenue, ownership and ownership changes, and ownership/workforce diversity, certifications, and formal inclusion policies (including subcontractors). It covers business-continuity and disaster recovery, security safeguards, cyber incidents and third-party assessments, and professional-liability coverage. Questions address opposition to FPIF or Illinois Public Act 101-0610; Illinois Article 3/4 pension advisory relationships at two specified dates; conflicts of interest; sustainability/ESG policies and UNPRI reporting; legal proceedings and regulatory discipline; SEC audit findings and responses; and the current auditor and date of last change.

nodes.title: Team
nodes.summary: The section requests information on firm and investment-professional headcounts, workforce diversity, and professionals researching or supporting private equity, private debt, infrastructure, and real estate. It covers research-department structure; proposed mandate leads and support staff, biographies, experience, tenure, client loads, FPIF meeting attendance, contact details, team size, market coverage, and reporting charts. It asks how team stability is maintained, analyst specialization is organized, staff are evaluated and compensated, and investment alignment is ensured. Firms must report overall and senior turnover, investment-professional departures since 2018, leadership and research personnel additions or departures over ten years, circumstances and planned exits, succession implementation, and anticipated retirements. It also requests client-service team roles, biographies and locations; employee public-office and investment-fund trustee service; the Chief Compliance Officer’s identity and biography; and whether legal services are provided in-house or externally, naming outside counsel.

nodes.title: Strategy, Process, and Performance
nodes.summary: The RFP requests detailed information from firms proposing private equity and/or private debt solutions. For private equity, it covers experience and investment universe; buyout, growth, venture, niche, co-investment, and secondary strategies; risk management, philosophy, sourcing, GP/fund selection, macro views, and investment, operational, and legal due diligence. It asks about commitments, fund counts, oversubscription and allocation policies, proprietary funds, staffing, GP relationships, LPAC participation, market outlook, competitive advantages and competitors, fee mitigation, return dispersion, manager access and databases, screening deliverables, and dated performance for specified strategy composites and benchmark comparisons. For private debt, it asks about experience, universe, strategy and lending segments, niche opportunities, risk management, proprietary funds, philosophy, due diligence, commitments and allocations, sourcing, staffing, relationships and LPACs, market outlook, advantages and competitors, fee mitigation, manager access and return dispersion, and representative performance. Pitchbooks, due-diligence checklist examples, allocation policies, and formatted performance tables are requested where applicable.

nodes.title: June 30, 2022.
nodes.summary: The text includes a June 30, 2022 performance-table template with fund size, investments, committed and invested capital, realized proceeds, unrealized and total value, returns and multiples, vintage, strategy, and performance periods; it also references a Private Debt Composite. The FPIF RFP then asks real-assets proposers (advisers or consultants) about: experience and assets managed in core/non-core real estate and infrastructure; investable universe and preferences; core/non-core strategy expertise and allocation recommendations; risk management, philosophy, public-market and macro influences, and GP selection; investment, operational, and legal due diligence, checklists, monitoring, and site visits; five-year commitments, fund counts, oversubscription, allocations, and capacity sharing; sourcing, staffing, GP relationships, fund history, and LPAC participation; market outlook, attractive sectors, portfolio positioning, and infrastructure benefits; strategy evaluation priorities and competitive advantages; competitors, fee and carry mitigation, and access to highly ranked managers; and flagship-fund or representative-composite performance, with a specified reporting format.

nodes.title: June 30, 2022.
nodes.summary: Dated June 30, 2022, this FPIF RFP Exhibit B1 requests performance information for Core and Non-Core Real Estate and Infrastructure composites, if available. A table should be completed for each composite, listing investments and vintage, fund size, committed and invested capital, realized proceeds, unrealized and total value, gross and net MOIC and IRR, DPI, RVPI, and TVPI. A second table requests strategy-level committed capital, number of funds, inception date, and 1-, 3-, 5-, 10-year and since-inception IRRs, including totals. Questions 56–57 ask whether asset-class capacity constraints or AUM limits apply to proposed mandates, and the sizes and inception dates of the five largest substantially similar consulting/advisory mandates from unique investors as of December 31, 2022, plus largest, smallest, average, and median client sizes.

nodes.title: Operations
nodes.summary: The questions ask whether the proposed strategies are available through separately managed accounts and whether minimum account sizes apply; expected turnaround for quarterly and annual performance reports; any significant compliance or ethics violations and their handling and resolution; the firm’s competitive advantages and reasons for selection; client tools for reporting, sourcing, and evaluating strategies; and a sample quarterly report. They also cover attribution capabilities for private-market portfolios and managers, including asset-class and manager-level analysis and online access. Firms must describe GP financial reporting requirements and procedures for reconciling investment valuations, commitments, paid-in and invested capital, distributions, expenses, management fees, and cash, including reconciliation of manager statements with client custodians. The questions additionally ask about fee monitoring or validation services and any remarks on the firm’s distinctive suitability as an FPIF partner.

result.title: Exhibit C: Minimum Qualifications Certification
result.summary: Exhibit C is a minimum-qualifications certification to complete, sign, and include with the proposal. The respondent certifies that it is a registered investment adviser or identifies its exemption; will serve as an Illinois Pension Code fiduciary if retained; holds all required authorizations and credentials; has a designated senior account professional with at least 10 years’ industry experience; manages at least $500 million and has five years of performance history in the proposed asset classes; has experience managing tax-exempt or governmental defined benefit plans; and has operated as an investment manager for at least 10 years, with time-based criteria measured as of December 31, 2022. The form includes fields for the company, authorized signer, title, and date. Respondents that do not meet every minimum requirement should not submit a proposal to FPIF.

result.title: Exhibit D: Form of Fee Proposal
result.summary:

Please provide a fee proposal for the proposed mandate(s). Consultants should propose a flat annual fee structure for private markets consulting. Consultants that offer both general consulting and private market consulting should also submit a joint fee proposal for both services. Discretionary Advisors should propose a flat fee or asset-based management fee. Incentive compensation will be considered.

result.title: Exhibit E: Additional Documentation and Data
result.summary: Exhibit E of the FPIF Request for Proposals requires respondents to attach all documents requested in Exhibit B and provide: ADV Part II; allocation policy; biographies of consultants, account leads, proposed senior personnel, and the Chief Compliance Officer; investment, operational, and legal due diligence checklists; code of ethics or professional conduct; corporate social responsibility, diversity, sustainability/ESG, disaster recovery, and business continuity policies or plans; a pitchbook or standard marketing presentation for proposed strategies; proof of E&O, professional liability, fiduciary, and other insurance coverage; a sample quarterly investment performance report; an SEC review findings letter; and, if applicable, state or local minority certification/registration and a GIPS verification letter.
